title: Character rig
description: A cut-out puppet: PNG parts carried by a bone hierarchy (D-027), per view. Lives at films/<film>/characters/<id>/rig.json. All positions are pixels in a part's own image (origin top-left, y down). The rest pose is the art as drawn: each bone points in its `direction_deg`, and motion angles are offsets from that rest pose. Structural rules JSON Schema cannot express (one root, no cycles, joints attach to the parent's part, draw order lists every part once) are checked by studio_core.schema.check_rig.

style.description: Style preset the art was made with (config/models.toml [styles], D-025).

views.description: One rig per view. Front is required for v1; three_quarter is optional.

id.description: Lowercase identifier: letters, digits, underscores; starts with a letter.

point_px.description: [x, y] in image pixels, origin top-left, y down.

root.description: Name of the root bone (usually the hips/torso). Its pivot is where the character stands.

draw_order.description: Part names from back to front. Independent of the bone hierarchy (a far arm can sit behind the torso).

bendable_limbs.description: Limbs that are drawn as ONE image and bend smoothly at the joint (arms, legs), instead of two rigid parts. Optional: a view without it is the plain two-part rig. Each limb replaces every part carried by its two bones: when the engine bends limbs, those parts are not drawn and the limb image is drawn in the earliest draw_order slot of them. The parts stay in the rig as the fallback (two rigid pieces, used when bending is switched off) and because a child joint (a hand) attaches to a part of its parent bone.

parent.description: Parent bone name, or null for the root bone.

attach.description: Where this bone's joint sits: a pixel in one of the parent bone's part images. Omitted for the root.

direction_deg.description: Rest direction of the bone in the drawn art, degrees counter-clockwise from +x: 90 = up (torso, head), -90 = down (hanging arms, legs).

length_px.description: Visible bone length, for drawing handles only.

side.description: The character's own left/right, for motions with a `side` parameter.

limits_deg.description: Allowed offset from the rest pose; motions and pose_at clamp to it.

follow.description: Optional tuning of the follow-through layer for a secondary bone (role `ear` or `tail`): the layer lags the bone behind its parent and lets it overshoot a little (studio_core.motions.follow). Every field is optional; the layer has defaults per role and scales them by the action's energy. Rigs without ear or tail bones never use it.

lag_s.description: How long the bone trails its parent's turn, in seconds.

damping.description: 0.2 swings several times, 0.5 overshoots a little, 1 does not overshoot.

gain.description: Scales the whole response; 0 switches follow-through off for this bone.

role.description: What the bone is, so named motions (wave, walk, nod...) can find it on any rig. Combined with `side` for limbs.

file.description: PNG path relative to the character folder, e.g. 'parts/torso.png'.

pivot_px.description: The pixel that sits on the bone's joint (it rotates around this point).

bone.description: The bone that carries this part.

face.description: Anchors for the procedural vector face (D-007), in pixels of `part` (the head image).

left_px.description: Centre of the character's left eye (on the viewer's right in the front view).

bendable_limb.description: One limb image bent along a two-bone chain. The image is the limb drawn straight in the rest pose (as the parts are drawn).

name.description: Limb name, unique in the view, e.g. 'arm_l'.

bones.description: [upper bone, lower bone]: the lower bone's parent is the upper bone, e.g. ['upper_arm_l', 'forearm_l'].

file.description: PNG path relative to the character folder, e.g. 'parts/arm_l.png'.

pivot_px.description: The pixel that sits on the first (upper) bone's joint, e.g. the shoulder.

joint_px.description: The pixel on the second joint (the elbow or knee), where the limb bends. Its offset from pivot_px must match the lower bone's `attach` offset in the rig (within a few pixels).
